lpic2-ldap-busqueda.title: Query the directory with a filter
lpic2-ldap-busqueda.briefing: The LDAP directory on `ldap-srv` (base `dc=lpic,dc=lab`) stores people in `ou=personas`. Using an anonymous search (simple bind), get the users whose `uidNumber` is 10003 or greater and save the output to `uids.txt`, which must contain, for each entry, only the `uid` attribute (the `dn` may appear) and no comments. The filter must be applied in the query itself. Your `ldap-srv` terminal opens in `/root/retos/ldap01`; `ldap-cli` is the client for the same directory.
lpic2-ldap-busqueda.blind_alert: REQUEST [DIRECTORY] · The list of users above a certain uidNumber needs to be extracted from the LDAP directory.
hints: `ldapsearch` accepts a parenthesized filter as an argument and a list of attributes to return at the end; there is an option to remove comments from the LDIF.
For anonymous simple bind, use `-x`; specify the base with `-b`, and `-LLL` leaves the LDIF without comments or version. The filter supports comparisons such as `>=`.
`ldapsearch -x -LLL -b ou=personas,dc=lpic,dc=lab '(uidNumber>=10003)' uid > uids.txt`
lpic2-ldap-busqueda.solution_summary: `ldapsearch -x -LLL` performs an anonymous search and suppresses comments; the filter `(uidNumber>=10003)` is evaluated on the server, and specifying `uid` at the end limits the attributes returned, so only those lines end up in `uids.txt`.

checks.uids.txt lista a todos los usuarios que: uids.txt lists all users that match the filter
checks.uids.txt no incluye a los que no lo cump: uids.txt does not include those that do not match

lpic2-ldap-nuevo-usuario.title: Add a user with ldapadd and log in via ssh
lpic2-ldap-nuevo-usuario.briefing: The LDAP directory on `ldap-srv` (base `dc=lpic,dc=lab`) stores people in `ou=personas`. Create an LDIF file with the user `sara` in `ou=personas` (objectClass `inetOrgPerson` and `posixAccount`; `uidNumber` 10010, `gidNumber` 10000, `homeDirectory` /home/sara, `loginShell` /bin/bash), add it with `ldapadd` as `cn=admin,dc=lpic,dc=lab` (password `admin`), and set the password `sara` with `ldappasswd`. Verify from `ldap-srv` that `sara` can log in via ssh to `ldap-cli` and that `/home/sara` is created. Your `ldap-srv` terminal opens in `/root/retos/ldap02`; `ldap-cli` is the client for the same directory.
lpic2-ldap-nuevo-usuario.blind_alert: REQUEST [DIRECTORY] · A user needs to be created and allowed to log in via ssh.
hints: `ldapadd` adds entries from an LDIF specified with `-f`; `ldappasswd` changes a user's password. Both use simple bind with `-x` and the directory administrator.

The administrator bind is `-D cn=admin,dc=lpic,dc=lab -w admin`. With `ldappasswd`, use `-s sara` to set the password. The `sssd` client may remember for a few seconds that the user did not exist; if the first attempt fails, run `sss_cache -E` on `ldap-cli` and retry.

On `ldap-srv`: `cat > sara.ldif <<'L' ... L` with the dn and attributes, then `ldapadd -x -D cn=admin,dc=lpic,dc=lab -w admin -f sara.ldif` and `ldappasswd -x -D cn=admin,dc=lpic,dc=lab -w admin -s sara uid=sara,ou=personas,dc=lpic,dc=lab`. On `ldap-cli`: `sss_cache -E`. And from `ldap-srv`: `sshpass -p sara ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o LogLevel=ERROR -o ConnectTimeout=10 sara@ldap-cli true`.
lpic2-ldap-nuevo-usuario.solution_summary: The LDIF declares the sara entry and `ldapadd` inserts it by authenticating as admin. `ldappasswd` sets the password so sara's bind works. When validating the login via ssh, `sssd` and `pam_mkhomedir` create the home directory on `ldap-cli`; if the `sssd` cache takes time to refresh, `sss_cache -E` forces the update.

checks.sara entra por ssh desde ldap-srv: sara logs in via ssh from ldap-srv
checks.se ha creado el directorio personal de s: sara's home directory has been created on the client

lpic2-ldap-grupo.title: Add a user to a group with ldapmodify
lpic2-ldap-grupo.briefing: The LDAP directory on `ldap-srv` (base `dc=lpic,dc=lab`) stores groups in `ou=grupos`. Using `ldapmodify` as `cn=admin,dc=lpic,dc=lab` (password `admin`), add `pedro` to the group `cn=admins,ou=grupos` (attribute `memberUid`). Verify from `ldap-cli` that `id pedro` shows the `admins` group. Your `ldap-srv` terminal opens in `/root/retos/ldap03`; `ldap-cli` is the client for the same directory.
lpic2-ldap-grupo.blind_alert: REQUEST [DIRECTORY] · A user needs to be added to an existing group.
hints: `ldapmodify` applies changes described in an LDIF; to add a value to a multivalued attribute, use `changetype: modify` and `add: memberUid`, followed by the line with the value.
The administrator bind is `-x -D cn=admin,dc=lpic,dc=lab -w admin`. The target dn is `cn=admins,ou=grupos,dc=lpic,dc=lab`.

`ldapmodify -x -D cn=admin,dc=lpic,dc=lab -w admin <<'L'
dn: cn=admins,ou=grupos,dc=lpic,dc=lab
changetype: modify
add: memberUid
memberUid: pedro
L`
lpic2-ldap-grupo.solution_summary: The LDIF modifies the group `admins` by adding `memberUid: pedro` without touching the existing values. The `sssd` client needs to refresh its cache with `sss_cache -E` for `id pedro` to reflect the new group.

checks.los miembros anteriores del grupo admins: the previous members of the admins group are preserved

lpic2-ldap-clave.title: Change a password with ldappasswd
lpic2-ldap-clave.briefing: In the LDAP directory on `ldap-srv` (base `dc=lpic,dc=lab`), change the password for user `luis` to `Nueva123` using `ldappasswd` as `cn=admin,dc=lpic,dc=lab` (password `admin`). Then `ldapwhoami` with `luis` and the new password must succeed, and with the old password (`luis`) it must fail. Your `ldap-srv` terminal opens in `/root/retos/ldap04`; `ldap-cli` is the client for the same directory.
lpic2-ldap-clave.blind_alert: REQUEST [DIRECTORY] · A user's LDAP password needs to be changed.
hints: `ldappasswd` changes the `userPassword` attribute of an entry; you can authenticate as the administrator to change another user's password.
For simple bind, use `-x -D cn=admin,dc=lpic,dc=lab -w admin -s Nueva123 uid=luis,ou=personas,dc=lpic,dc=lab`.
`ldappasswd -x -D cn=admin,dc=lpic,dc=lab -w admin -s Nueva123 uid=luis,ou=personas,dc=lpic,dc=lab`
lpic2-ldap-clave.solution_summary: `ldappasswd` authenticated as admin updates `userPassword` for luis, so the bind with the new password succeeds and the old password is rejected. The test with `ldapwhoami` verifies the authenticated identity.

lpic2-ldap-indice.title: Add an index for mail in cn=config
lpic2-ldap-indice.briefing: On the LDAP server `ldap-srv`, using `ldapmodify -Y EXTERNAL -H ldapi:///`, modify the database `olcDatabase={1}mdb,cn=config` and add an equality index (`eq`) for the `mail` attribute (`olcDbIndex`). Verify with `ldapsearch` on `cn=config` that this index appears and that the previous indexes remain present. Your `ldap-srv` terminal opens in `/root/retos/ldap05`; `ldap-cli` is the client for the same directory.
lpic2-ldap-indice.blind_alert: REQUEST [DIRECTORY] · An equality index for mail needs to be added to the LDAP database.
hints: `ldapmodify -Y EXTERNAL -H ldapi:///` allows modifying the `cn=config` database; indexes are stored in the multivalued attribute `olcDbIndex`.
The target dn is `olcDatabase={1}mdb,cn=config`; the change is `add: olcDbIndex` followed by `olcDbIndex: mail eq`.

`ldapmodify -Q -Y EXTERNAL -H ldapi:/// <<'L'
dn: olcDatabase={1}mdb,cn=config
changetype: modify
add: olcDbIndex
olcDbIndex: mail eq
L`
lpic2-ldap-indice.solution_summary: Adds `olcDbIndex: mail eq` to the mdb database; OpenLDAP will start maintaining an equality index for the `mail` attribute without removing the existing indexes because `add` does not replace. Verification on `cn=config` and a search by `mail` confirm the change.

checks.los índices anteriores de la base se con: the previous indexes of the database are preserved
checks.las búsquedas por mail devuelven la entr: searches by mail return the entry

lpic2-ldap-slapcat.title: Backup with slapcat and slapd stopped
lpic2-ldap-slapcat.briefing: On `ldap-srv`, stop `slapd` with `slapd-ctl stop` (this container has no `systemctl`), export the `dc=lpic,dc=lab` database with `slapcat` to `/root/retos/ldap06/copia.ldif`, and start `slapd` again with `slapd-ctl start`. Verify that it responds. Your `ldap-srv` terminal opens in `/root/retos/ldap06`; `ldap-cli` is the client for the same directory.
lpic2-ldap-slapcat.blind_alert: REQUEST [DIRECTORY] · An LDIF copy of the directory must be made with the service stopped.
hints: This container uses `slapd-ctl` instead of systemd; the basic operations are `stop`, `start`, `restart`, and `status`.
`slapcat` must be run with the service stopped and accepts `-b` for the base and `-l` for the output file.
`slapd-ctl stop && slapcat -b dc=lpic,dc=lab -l /root/retos/ldap06/copia.ldif && slapd-ctl start`
lpic2-ldap-slapcat.solution_summary: With `slapd` stopped, `slapcat` dumps the indicated database in LDIF format consistently. Then the service is started again so it keeps responding. The check validates that the file contains the expected entries and that the server is running again.

lpic2-ldap-tls.title: Query with StartTLS (-ZZ) and with ldaps://
lpic2-ldap-tls.briefing: On `ldap-srv`, run two queries and save their output: with StartTLS (option `-ZZ`) get `carol`'s `mail` and save it to `/root/retos/ldap07/starttls.txt`; with `ldaps://` get `ana`'s `dn` and save it to `/root/retos/ldap07/ldaps.txt`. Also save the Subject of the server certificate to `/root/retos/ldap07/cert.txt` (use `openssl s_client` on port 636). Your `ldap-srv` terminal opens in `/root/retos/ldap07`; `ldap-cli` is the client for the same directory.
lpic2-ldap-tls.blind_alert: REQUEST [DIRECTORY] · The directory needs to be queried using StartTLS and LDAPS, and the certificate extracted.
hints: `ldapsearch` accepts `-ZZ` to require StartTLS and `-H ldaps://ldap-srv` for LDAPS; in both cases `-x` performs a simple bind.
For the certificate, `openssl s_client -connect ldap-srv:636 </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -subject` extracts the Subject.

`ldapsearch -x -LLL -ZZ -H ldap://ldap-srv "(uid=carol)" mail > /root/retos/ldap07/starttls.txt` · `ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldaps://ldap-srv "(uid=ana)" dn > /root/retos/ldap07/ldaps.txt` · `openssl s_client -connect ldap-srv:636 </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -subject > /root/retos/ldap07/cert.txt`
lpic2-ldap-tls.solution_summary: The server has StartTLS and LDAPS configured with its certificate. `ldapsearch -ZZ` forces StartTLS and `-H ldaps://` uses encrypted port 636; both return only what was requested, and the output is redirected to the files. `openssl s_client` shows the certificate and `openssl x509 -subject` extracts the CN.

checks.cert.txt contiene el Subject real del ce: cert.txt contains the actual Subject of the server certificate

lpic2-ldap-acl.title: An ACL: mail only for authenticated users
lpic2-ldap-acl.briefing: On `ldap-srv`, any anonymous client can currently read the `mail` attribute. Using `ldapmodify -Y EXTERNAL -H ldapi:///`, modify `olcDatabase={1}mdb,cn=config` and add an `olcAccess` rule that allows reading `mail` only to authenticated users (`by users read`) and nothing to the rest (`by * none`). It must be FIRST (`{0}`). Then, without `-D/-w` the `mail` of `carol` must not be visible; with `ana/ana` it must be. And `userPassword` remains protected for that user. Your `ldap-srv` terminal opens in `/root/retos/ldap08`; `ldap-cli` is the client for the same directory.
lpic2-ldap-acl.blind_alert: REQUEST [DIRECTORY] · Mail reading needs to be restricted so that only authenticated users can do it.
hints: OpenLDAP ACLs are managed in `cn=config` with `olcAccess`; order matters and `{0}` places the rule at the beginning.
The target dn is `olcDatabase={1}mdb,cn=config`; the rule is `olcAccess: {0}to attrs=mail by users read by * none`.

`ldapmodify -Q -Y EXTERNAL -H ldapi:/// <<'L'
dn: olcDatabase={1}mdb,cn=config
changetype: modify
add: olcAccess
olcAccess: {0}to attrs=mail by users read by * none
L`
lpic2-ldap-acl.solution_summary: By adding the ACL `{0}to attrs=mail by users read by * none`, rules are evaluated in order and this one is first: it grants `mail` only to authenticated users and denies the rest. The previous rules (`userPassword` protected and general reading) remain active, so authenticated `ana` sees `carol`'s `mail` but not her `userPassword`.

checks.la regla de mail es la primera ACL ({0}): the mail rule is the first ACL ({0}) of the mdb database
checks.un cliente anónimo no ve el mail de caro: an anonymous client does not see carol's mail
checks.un cliente anónimo sigue viendo el uid d: an anonymous client still sees carol's uid

lpic2-ldap-pam-access.title: PAM on the client: only the admins group can log in via ssh
lpic2-ldap-pam-access.briefing: On `ldap-cli` (as root), using `pam_access` you must allow only `root` and the `admins` group to log in via ssh; everyone else must be rejected. Enable `pam_access` in the sshd account stack (`/etc/pam.d/sshd`, line `account required pam_access.so`) and in `/etc/security/access.conf` add allow rules for `root` and `(admins)` before a deny-all rule. Result: `ana` (admins) logs in via ssh; `luis` (not admins) is rejected even if the password is correct. To test access, use `sshpass` from `ldap-srv` against `ldap-cli`. Your `ldap-cli` terminal opens in `/root`; `ldap-srv` is the directory server.
lpic2-ldap-pam-access.blind_alert: REQUEST [DIRECTORY] · SSH access with PAM needs to be configured so that only the admins group can log in.
hints: `pam_access` is enabled by adding `account required pam_access.so` to `/etc/pam.d/sshd`; the rules go in `/etc/security/access.conf`.
Access rules are written as `+:` (allow) and `-:` (deny). A group is indicated with parentheses: `+:(admins):ALL`.
In `/etc/security/access.conf` add `+:root:ALL`, `+:(admins):ALL`, and `-:ALL:ALL`. In `/etc/pam.d/sshd`, insert `account required pam_access.so` before `@include common-account` if it is not there.
lpic2-ldap-pam-access.solution_summary: With `pam_access` active in the sshd account stack, the `access.conf` rules are evaluated in order: first root and the admins group are allowed, then everyone is denied. Since `ana` is a member of admins, her ssh access works, while `luis` receives the denial. The rule order prevents the deny rule from blocking the allowed ones.

checks.access.conf permite a root y al grupo ad: access.conf allows root and the admins group before denying everyone else
checks.ana (admins) entra por ssh desde ldap-sr: ana (admins) logs in via ssh from ldap-srv
checks.luis (no admins) es rechazado por ssh: luis (not admins) is rejected by ssh

lpic2-ldap-mkhomedir.title: PAM: create home directories with 750 permissions (pam_mkhomedir)
lpic2-ldap-mkhomedir.briefing: On `ldap-cli`, the home directories created by `pam_mkhomedir` currently come out with mode 700. Edit `/etc/pam.d/common-session` and configure `pam_mkhomedir` with the `umask=0027` option so that new home directories get mode 750. Log in for the first time as `marta` (password `marta`) from `ldap-srv` using `sshpass` so that `/home/marta` is created; it must end up with mode 750. Your `ldap-cli` terminal opens in `/root`; `ldap-srv` is the directory server.
lpic2-ldap-mkhomedir.blind_alert: REQUEST [DIRECTORY] · Configure pam_mkhomedir so home directories are created with 750 permissions.
hints: `pam_mkhomedir.so` accepts the `umask=0027` option, which yields `0777 - 0027 = 0750`.
The line to modify is in `/etc/pam.d/common-session`; use `sed` to add `umask=0027` to `pam_mkhomedir.so`.

On `ldap-cli`: `sed -i 's/^\(session[[:space:]]\+optional[[:space:]]\+pam_mkhomedir.so\).*/\1 umask=0027/' /etc/pam.d/common-session`. Then, from `ldap-srv`: `sshpass -p marta ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o LogLevel=ERROR -o ConnectTimeout=10 marta@ldap-cli true`.
lpic2-ldap-mkhomedir.solution_summary: The `umask=0027` option of `pam_mkhomedir` makes the directory be created with `0777 & ~0027 = 0750`. When `marta` logs in over ssh, PAM creates her home directory with those permissions. The check validates the configuration and the directory properties.
